lines.text: One of the biggest reasons early solo work gets stressful isn't that the offer is bad.
It's that there's no system around it.
You don't need a complicated business operating system to begin.
You need a few simple pieces.
First, a place to track who you're talking to and what stage each opportunity is in.
This can be as simple as a spreadsheet, a Notion board, or a document.
If someone says yes, what happens next? What questions do you ask; what information do you need; what do you send?
Proposal language, follow-up emails, meeting agendas, project checklists; templates save you time and keep your work consistent.
One hour a week to look at your outreach, your active work, your admin, and your next steps keeps solo work from turning reactive.
And finally, boundaries: how many hours will you give this?
What kinds of work are out of scope?
What kinds of clients or timelines aren't a fit?
AI can help you build templates and organize information, but the boundaries are still your call.
In this module, you'll define your time budget, choose a few systems to build now, and decide where you need guardrails before your path grows.
